body:
CANONICAL: restart rules, review cadence and a temporary model workaround for Engram (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03; split from rules-authority-and-landing for size; rev 6 on 2026-10-29 replaces the restart-release and restart-reporting parts with a pointer to rules-install-and-cutover item 5). The controlling text is AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (Authority and Git, Review Cadence) and .claude/commands/review-changes.md. Read the current text when acting. This note records Greg's words and agreed readings, and carries no higher authority than his current word.

RESTARTS (Greg, 2026-10-02 in Advisor session-6219: "Wolę aby agenci zdecydowali na moment restaru Termal. Wtedy kiedy potrzebuja poprawek. To nie jest problem, nie chce przerywać pracy." and "Chwila. Termal muszę zrestartować ja. Engram mogą sami. Wiec do restaru termala oczekuje od nich potwierdzenia kiedy potrzebują to zrobic."). TermAl: Greg performs every TermAl restart; its MOMENT is the agents'. The Engram and TermAl coordinators agree a moment when running work can resume: no full gate mid-run, no reviewer children alive, no landing or install in progress, no recognised test turn mid-run, no evaluation delegation running, every coordinator told. The RELEASE SEQUENCE AND ITS WORDING (Greg's window as the readiness word, INSTALL NOW, verified INSTALLED, the final RESTART NOW via Advisor naming the installed Engram build and the intended TermAl main commit, the Polish HOLD line until then, rollback and post-restart checks) are in rules-install-and-cutover item 5, the one current recipe. No agent stops or starts the TermAl host. Agents keep working while a restart is pending: no held window, no pausing; work a restart cuts is recovered or rerun. Engram: agents may restart Engram's own processes themselves, only by a supported route. There is no restart command: let a TermAl control sidecar go 5 minutes without control requests (TermAl reaps it and starts the installed build on the next request; the reap is per session), or start a new CLI process. An `engram mcp` server refreshes only when its host session is recreated, which for TermAl sessions means Greg's TermAl restart. NEVER kill any engram.exe process, least of all a live `engram mcp` server: Claude Code does not reconnect a killed stdio MCP server. A new control connection expires issued-but-unbegun grants; begun turns stay open. These rules are in the checked-in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (Authority and Git) since commit 7dd5195 (2026-10-03, item w-06009c591bbb): the standing approval still grants no restart, deploy or global-configuration authority, and only Greg's quoted words grant the TermAl-moment and Engram-route exceptions. Read that text when acting. Deploy and global configuration stay Greg's and need his explicit word.

REVIEW CADENCE (Greg, 2026-09-26, committed 7424da9; adopted coordination rules of 2026-09-13 revision 1 in docs/agent-pair-workflow.md). One parent owns each review input: it runs the gates, freezes, obtains exactly the Codex and Claude pair read-only, consolidates and records. The gate and both reviews run in parallel on one frozen input, and a failed gate discards those reviews. Fix rounds keep both reviewers. Before coding an item: a design review with Engram::Fable and a read-only Codex explorer. During a gate or review, only non-mutating work on the next item. Repeat verification only for a changed input or a concrete failure, recovering existing results first. Report outcomes, blockers and decisions, not ACK chains. TermAl owns the tests of its host safeguards (denied writes, interpreter restrictions); they block an Engram review only with a concrete connection to the review's access or integrity. Kimi's optional third review stays PAUSED (Greg's word relayed to Engram::Opus as mailbox #587) until Greg lifts it; when it lifts, AGENTS.md's paragraph on the optional third review applies (never counted, never blocking, none on a finished round, a justified Medium or higher fixed and reviewed again by the pair). The Kimi stand-in for an unavailable Codex or Claude reviewer (at most one per round, never for both; commit d10f724, see rules-throughput) is a separate rule and not paused.

CLAUDE MODEL AVAILABILITY (since 2026-10-02 about 23:25Z): a weekly usage limit refused some Claude sessions and default-model reviewer spawns; availability varies by model and time. Pass the model explicitly on every Claude reviewer or evaluator spawn, try another if one is refused, and record each refusal on the item: a recorded Claude refusal is what admits the Kimi stand-in. The pair rule names vendors, not models.

REPORTING THE TERMAL RESTART: follow rules-install-and-cutover item 5. Don't name a TermAl build hash from memory in Greg-facing text. The restart input is the intended TermAl main commit, and the running hash after start is only a confirmation (Greg #2285). Keep a RESTART NOW (the final release) separate from status or readiness notices, which begin with the HOLD line until the release.
